claim.purpose: Keep typed C-SDLC lifecycle writes rooted in the bound issue worktree

initial.title: [v0.91.8][csdlc-v2][tooling] Keep all issue lifecycle writes in the bound worktree
initial.goal: Make typed C-SDLC v2 lifecycle writes materialize and operate from the declared bound worktree instead of dirtying the primary checkout.
initial.required_outcome: Binding and later doctor/validate/review/publish/closeout use the same issue worktree root, while primary-main lifecycle writes fail closed outside explicit bootstrap/read-only paths.
authority_boundary: Issue #5658 owns only typed v2 lifecycle-root behavior and focused regressions
Existing issue records and #5655 are preserved
Root main cleanup is not part of implementation
operator_constraints: Rust binaries only; no Python or shell lifecycle wrapper
initial.task_boundary: Implement the bounded C-SDLC v2 lifecycle-root repair and prove it with focused Rust tests.
deliverables: Fail-closed guard for unsafe primary-main lifecycle writes
Regression covering ignored .csdlc state in a newly-created worktree
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: csdlc-bind materializes or verifies issue record, cards, lock, prepared artifacts, and evidence root in the declared bound worktree
AC-2: write attempts against primary main fail closed unless explicitly bootstrap/read-only
AC-3: bound-worktree doctor, validate, review, publish, and closeout use the same repository root as implementation
AC-4: a regression covers a newly-created worktree where .csdlc paths are ignored or absent
AC-5: claim, lock, and exact-revision protections remain strict
dependencies: Issue #5655 typed GitHub action surface remains preserved
non_goals: No manual copying of existing issue records
No cleanup of root #5671 artifacts in this issue
No weakening claim, lock, or exact-revision protections
initial.plan_summary: Read the current v2 lifecycle root handling, add the smallest root/materialization guard and regression, run focused Rust tests on FastWork, perform exact-head review, publish, merge, and close out.

steps.action: Inspect current bind/store lifecycle root behavior and locate the unsafe primary-main write path
Implement bound-worktree materialization and fail-closed primary-main guard
Add focused regression for newly-created worktree with ignored or absent .csdlc state
Run focused FastWork validation, review, publish, merge, and closeout

invariants: The implementation root and lifecycle root must match after binding
Primary checkout on main must remain clean for non-bootstrap issue execution
Existing claim, lock, and exact-revision protections stay fail-closed
risks: Overbroad main-write guard could block legitimate bootstrap or read-only operations
Materialization could accidentally fork lifecycle truth instead of moving it to the bound root
Regression may need careful temp/worktree isolation to avoid local disk writes
stop_conditions: Fix requires rewriting historical issue records
Fix requires weakening claim, lock, or exact-revision checks
FastWork is unavailable for worktree or Rust output
Scope expands beyond typed v2 lifecycle roots

validation_lanes.proof_role: Prove bound-worktree lifecycle materialization and fail-closed primary-main behavior

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on any lifecycle-root ambiguity, root-main write attempt outside explicit bootstrap/read-only operation, stale claim, stale digest, lock mismatch, or exact-revision mismatch.
review_prompts: Can any execution-phase typed command still write issue lifecycle state to primary main after binding?
Does the regression prove absent ignored .csdlc state is materialized into the bound worktree?
Were claim, lock, and exact-revision protections preserved without broad bypasses?
